Create the artwork that will be used for your pieces in 17x17 and 34x34 proportions. You can also import images, which will be automatically converted to the grid.

After creating your artwork, turn it into a board piece.
This piece represents the movement you just created.

With your pieces ready, it’s time to build your squad.
Arrange the pieces on the board however you like and define which one will be the King.

In the lobby, select which squads will play as black and white pieces by clicking on the board.
Then choose which one you will play with, indicated by the crown color.
Additional game options are available in the top-right corner.

Now it’s time to play the match.
In the top-left corner, you can surrender if the situation becomes difficult.
In the top-right corner are the view options.
On the right side of the screen, you can follow the match history.
This eraser allows you to quickly erase large areas of pixels of the same color.

To use the circle, rectangle, line, or selection tools, click on two points on the grid.
On PC, the small dot in the top-left corner indicates the mouse position.

After selecting an area, use the arrows in the bottom-left corner to move it.
Press the center button to confirm the movement and finish the tool.

The quick save button is used for artwork that has already been saved or loaded.
The set it belongs to will be displayed just below the button.

When clicking Save, the available sets will be shown next. Click the desired set again to confirm saving.
In the top-right corner, you can create a new set.
To delete, click Delete, select the desired set, and confirm the action.

Each color shows what the piece can do on that square.
Green: movement only.
Red: capture only.
Yellow: movement + capture.
Blue: jump movement.
Purple: jump + capture.

In Moves, you shape how the piece behaves on the board.
Define how far it can go, which directions it can move, and what type of action the move allows.
Each adjustment changes the strategy and creates new gameplay possibilities.

The special move is a unique ability of the Pawn that can only be used once.
Just like the Knight’s custom movement, simply select the desired squares and activate the move.

After finishing a piece, use the Reset button to clear the data and create a new piece from scratch.
Warning: creating a new piece without resetting and using Quick Save will overwrite the previous piece.

When clicking Save, the available sets will be shown next. Click the desired set again to confirm saving.
In the top-right corner, you can create a new set.
To delete, click Delete, select the desired set, and confirm the action.

When pressing Add, the available sets will be displayed.
Choose a set to add all of its pieces at once.
To add pieces individually, use the Pieces button in the top-right corner.

When no piece or button is selected, your squad information appears in the center of the screen.
There you can see the total number of pieces, the squad power, and which piece is the King.

Use the crown button to choose which piece will be the King of your squad.
Use the X button to remove a piece from the board.

Select a piece on the right side to see its information in the center of the screen.
Then simply click on the board position where you want to place it.

Use the + button to configure promotions and castling for the selected piece.
Simply drag the desired pieces.
Very powerful pieces have limitations: above 25 power they cannot promote, and above 80 power they cannot castle.

The messages displayed below the board indicate the status of Strategic Mode. This mode evaluates whether your squad is balanced compared to a classic chess set. Although it is possible to save and play with squads outside this standard, Strategic Mode is recommended to ensure greater competitiveness.

During Local Multiplayer, the board can automatically rotate each turn.
Use the icon in the top-right corner to enable or disable this rotation.
The crowns represent the two squads: the black squad at the top and the white squad at the bottom. The highlighted crown shows which squad you will control in the match.

Remember: you are a Human, the top crown is yours.
It represents you and the squad you will command in the match.
The pieces displayed on the side can be selected to view their moves, abilities, and which piece is defined as the king.

In No Rules mode, you are not required to protect the king when in check.
If you fail to notice it, the responsibility is yours, game over.

In No Turns mode, the match is played in real time.
Move your pieces freely without waiting for your opponent’s turn.
